instruction: I'd like you to access the Composition & Addressing settings in Thunderbird. Please open this configuration page so I can adjust email composition preferences.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening the Composition & Addressing settings tab in Thunderbird. The evaluator checks the accessibility tree for a tab named 'Composition & Addressing'. This follows the same navigation pattern as the original profile manager task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator semantically verifies the instruction correctly: checks for existence of 'Composition & Addressing' tab in Thunderbird's tab list via accessibility tree
Complete coverage: instruction requires opening the settings page, evaluator verifies the tab exists (which confirms successful opening)
Correct data flow: get_accessibility_tree extracts accessibility tree from Thunderbird UI, check_accessibility_tree applies CSS selector to find the target tab

CSS selector is semantically correct: targets 'application[name=Thunderbird] page-tab-list[attr|id="tabmail-tabs"]>page-tab[name="Composition & Addressing"]' which precisely identifies the settings tab
Logic is sound and will work at runtime: check_accessibility_tree function (general.py:216-267) properly handles CSS selectors, returns 0.0 if no match, 1.0 if match found

Postconfig is comprehensive and robust: re-navigates to the exact settings page (Ctrl+Comma to open preferences, Ctrl+F to search, types 'Composition & Addressing', presses Return) ensuring correct UI state before evaluation
No state timing issues: postconfig ensures the tab is open and active before evaluation runs, includes appropriate sleep delays for UI transitions
Getter can extract needed state: get_accessibility_tree is a standard, reliable method for extracting Thunderbird UI state via accessibility API
